steps: Cook the bulgur according to the package instructions, or soak it in hot water for 20 minutes. Let cool.
Finely chop the parsley, mint, tomatoes, cucumber, and spring onions.
Combine the bulgur with the vegetables.
Add the oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, and toss.
Chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Soaking the bread: Soak the 4 slices of stale bread (crusts removed) in water for a few minutes until softened. Stale bread binds better and gives the taramosalata a light, fluffy texture.
Squeezing: Squeeze the bread very well with your hands to remove all the water. Important: if any water remains, the taramosalata will turn out watery and won't come together.
Base in the blender: Place the 100g tarama, the squeezed bread, and the 1 small grated onion in the blender and blend until combined into a smooth paste.

Adding oil and lemon: Pour in the 150ml olive oil in a very thin stream, alternating with the 2 tbsp lemon juice, while the blender runs continuously. The slow stream of oil creates an emulsion and keeps the mixture combined.
Whipping until fluffy: Continue blending until it becomes a fluffy, uniform cream. Taste and adjust the lemon to your liking.
Resting in the fridge: Refrigerate the taramosalata for at least 1 hour before serving. The chilling firms up the texture and lets the flavors meld.
taramosalata.plate: In a bowl with olive oil and olives, lagana bread on the side.

steps: Blind baking the crust: Roll out the tart dough into the pan, prick the base with a fork and blind bake (with pie weights or dried beans) for 15 minutes, then another 5 minutes without weights at 180°C. Important: blind baking keeps the dough from puffing up and keeps the base crisp so it doesn't get soggy from the cream.
Cooling the base: Let the base cool completely before adding the cream. If it's still warm, the pastry cream will melt and turn runny.
Spreading the cream: Spread the cold pastry cream evenly over the base with a spatula, so each slice has an even layer.
Arranging the strawberries: Slice the 400g strawberries and arrange them attractively in circles or concentric rings over the cream. An even arrangement gives an impressive appearance.
Glazing: Gently brush fruit glaze over the strawberries for a glossy finish and to keep the fruit from oxidizing and drying out.
Chilling and serving: Refrigerate the tart for 1 hour so it sets and slices cleanly. Just before serving, dust with powdered sugar.

ing: Filling: Eggs 3, Sugar 150g, Juice of 3 lemons, Zest of 2 lemons, Butter 80g
steps: Dough: Cut the cold butter into cubes and rub into the flour and sugar until crumbly. Add the egg and knead minimally. Important: don't let the dough warm up — cold butter makes the crust crisp.
Chilling: Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Tart shell: Roll out thinly into a tart pan and prick with a fork. Line with parchment and fill with weights (beans). Blind bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, remove the weights, and bake for another 5 minutes.
Filling: Whisk the eggs with the sugar, add the lemon juice, zest, and cream. Heat over a bain-marie, stirring, until it thickens slightly (82°C). Stir in the butter.
Final baking: Pour the filling into the tart shell. Bake at 160°C for 20-25 minutes — the filling should still have a slight wobble in the center.
Cooling: Let it cool completely before slicing.
tarta_lemoni.plate: In thin slices with a little cream.

ing: Fresh yeast 20 g or dry 7 g
steps: Activating the yeast: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in a little lukewarm water and leave it for 10 minutes until it foams.
Important: The water must be lukewarm, never hot. Above 45°C the yeast dies and the batter never rises.
Making the batter: Mix the flour with the salt, add the yeast mixture and the rest of the water, whisking to a smooth thick batter.
Rising: Cover the bowl with a towel and leave it in a warm spot for 1 hour, until it has doubled and the surface is covered in bubbles.
Important: Do not stir the batter after it has risen. Those bubbles are the whole structure — stirring collapses them and the tiganites come out flat.
Heating the oil: Heat plenty of oil in a deep pan to 175°C. Tiganites must float, so the oil should be at least 3 cm deep.
Testing: Drop in a little batter — it should rise to the surface immediately and puff up.
Frying: Drop in spoonfuls with an oiled spoon, without crowding the pan.
Cooking: Fry for 2 minutes per side, until deep golden and puffed, turning once.
Draining and serving: Drain on a rack and serve at once, drizzled with honey and dusted with cinnamon and chopped walnuts.
tiganites_ellinikes.plate: Serve piping hot, drizzled with honey and dusted with cinnamon and walnuts.

steps: Cut the eggplants into 1cm slices. Salt them and let sit for 20 minutes. Pat dry.
Coat each slice in flour.
Fry in hot oil for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Remove onto paper towels.
Serve topped with grated garlic, vinegar, and salt.
Cutting: Peel the 4 medium potatoes and cut them into thick slices or cubes, so they stay crispy outside and fluffy inside.
Drying: Important: dry the potatoes very well with paper towels, since moisture causes the oil to spatter and prevents them from crisping.
Frying: Heat plenty of oil over high heat and fry the potatoes for 12-15 minutes, turning them so they brown evenly on all sides.
Draining: Remove them with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Salting and serving: Salt with coarse salt immediately while hot, so the salt sticks, and sprinkle with oregano if you like. Serve immediately.
tiganites_patates.plate: Piping hot, with oregano, alongside tzatziki or ketchup.

steps: Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Add the mascarpone and fold in gently.
Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks and fold them gently into the mixture.
Mix the espresso with the liqueur in a shallow bowl.
Quickly dip the ladyfingers (1-2 seconds per side) and arrange them in a baking dish.
Spread half the cream over the ladyfingers. Add another layer of ladyfingers, then the remaining cream.
Dust with cocoa and chill for 4-6 hours.
Choosing the ingredients: Let the cheeses come to room temperature so they blend more easily and evenly in the blender.
Blending the cheeses: Put the 200g feta, the 150g anthotyro or katiki cheese, the 3 tbsp olive oil, and the 1 clove of garlic in the blender. Blend until it forms a smooth, creamy paste.
Prepping the peppers: Finely chop the 2-3 hot peppers. Important: remove the seeds and membranes if you want less heat, since that's where most of the capsaicin is concentrated.
Combining: Fold the chopped peppers into the creamy mixture with a spoon (not in the blender), so bits remain and the spicy feta dip keeps some texture.
Adjusting the seasoning: Taste and add salt and pepper if needed, keeping in mind that the feta is already salty.
Resting: Refrigerate the spicy feta dip for at least 30 minutes before serving, so the texture sets and the flavors meld.
tirokafteri.plate: In a bowl, drizzled with olive oil, garnished with hot pepper, served with pita.

steps: Preparing the tomatoes: Cut the tomatoes, remove the seeds and squeeze them well to drain the liquid. Chop finely or coarsely grate them. Important: if you don't squeeze them well enough, the mixture will turn watery.
Mixture: Combine the tomato, finely chopped onion, parsley, mint, salt and pepper. Add the flour gradually until you get a thick mixture you can shape. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Frying: Heat oil in a pan. Drop spoonfuls of the mixture and press lightly to flatten. Fry for 3-4 minutes per side over medium heat until golden.
Serving: Place on paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve hot with tzatziki or yogurt.
tomatokeftedes.plate: Hot, with tzatziki or yogurt on the side.

steps: Prepping the bread: Lightly butter one side of each of the 4 bread slices using the 10g butter or margarine. The butter helps the outside turn crispy and golden.

Filling: Divide the 80g gouda or Emmental cheese and the 80g ham between the slices. Important: place cheese both above and below the ham, so that as it melts it seals the sandwich shut and it doesn't fall apart.
Closing the sandwich: Close the sandwich with the buttered side facing out, so it makes contact with the hot surface and browns.
Grilling: Grill in a sandwich press or a pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side, until the cheese melts and the bread turns crispy and golden.
Serving: Cut the sandwich diagonally and serve immediately while the cheese is melted and the outside is crispy.
Make the syrup first: boil the sugar, water, lemon and cinnamon for 8 minutes, then set it aside to cool completely.
Important: The syrup must be cold and the touloumbes hot. This contrast is what lets them absorb syrup without going soggy.
Bring the water and butter to the boil, then tip in the flour and semolina all at once.
Stir vigorously over the heat for 3-4 minutes, until the dough comes away from the sides and forms a ball.
Let it cool for 15 minutes. Important: adding eggs to hot dough cooks them into scrambled lumps.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating hard after each until the dough is smooth and glossy again.
Pipe 6 cm lengths through a star nozzle straight into oil at 160°C — a lower temperature than usual, so they cook through inside.
Fry slowly for 6-8 minutes, turning them, until deep golden all over. Rushing this leaves them raw in the middle.
Lift them straight from the oil into the cold syrup and leave them for 1 minute.
Drain them on a rack and serve with cinnamon.
touloumpes.plate: Serve on a platter with the syrup glistening and a dusting of cinnamon.

steps: Preparing the vegetables: Cut the eggplants and zucchini into thick rounds, the potatoes into slices, the peppers into strips, and the onions into half-moons. Important: salt the eggplant and let it sit in a colander for 20 minutes to release its bitter liquid, then rinse and dry it, so it doesn't turn bitter or soak up too much oil.
Arranging the pan: Grease a large baking pan and spread all the vegetables out, mixed together, so they cook evenly and share their flavors.
Tomato and garlic: Grate or finely chop the tomatoes and garlic cloves and scatter them over the vegetables along with half the parsley.
Seasoning: Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with salt, pepper, and oregano, and toss gently by hand to coat everything in the oil.
Baking covered: Cover the pan with foil and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 45 minutes, until the vegetables soften and release their juices.
Browning: Remove the foil, raise the temperature to 200°C, and continue baking for another 25-30 minutes, until nicely browned and most of the liquid has been absorbed.

Resting and serving: Remove the pan from the oven, sprinkle with the remaining fresh parsley, and let it rest for 10-15 minutes. Important: tourlou tastes best served warm or at room temperature, once the flavors have settled.
tourlou.plate: Serve with feta cheese and fresh bread for dipping into the juices.

steps: Base: Crush the biscuits in a food processor into crumbs and mix with the melted butter and a pinch of salt.
Shaping the base: Spread the mixture into a 22 cm ring lined with parchment paper on the bottom, pressing down firmly with the back of a spoon. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Hydrating the gelatin: Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes, squeeze out the excess water, and melt them in a little warm cream.
Important: The gelatin must be just lukewarm when folded into the hazelnut spread and cream cheese mixture, so it neither curdles the cream nor sets prematurely into lumps.
Hazelnut cream: Beat the cream cheese with the powdered sugar until fluffy, add the spread and mix until smooth, then stir in the gelatin.
Whipping the cream: Whip the remaining heavy cream to a medium-firm texture and gently fold it into the hazelnut mixture with bottom-to-top motions so as not to lose air.
Filling: Spread the cream over the base, smooth the surface with a spatula, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Decoration: Carefully unmold, dust the surface with cocoa, and scatter coarsely chopped toasted hazelnuts around the edge.
Serving: Cut with a knife dipped in hot water for clean slices.
tourta_fountoukiou.plate: Serve on a plate with a little cocoa dusted around and a spoonful of whipped cream alongside

steps: Preparing the oven: Preheat the oven to 175°C (fan) and butter two 22 cm round pans.
Beating the butter and sugar: Beat the butter with the sugar in a mixer until light and pale, about 5 minutes.
Adding the eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition so they are fully incorporated.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a separate bowl, sift the flour with the baking powder and add the shredded coconut.
Important: Alternately fold the dry ingredients and the milk into the butter mixture, starting and ending with the dry ingredients, mixing gently so as not to lose air and to keep the batter light.
Baking: Divide the batter between the two pans and bake for 30-35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Filling cream: Whip the heavy cream with the powdered sugar and coconut milk until firm and whipped.
Assembly: Once the sponge layers have cooled completely, fill and cover them with the coconut cream.
Decoration: Sprinkle generously with extra shredded coconut over the whole surface and sides of the cake.
Chilling and serving: Let the cake chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before cutting, so the cream sets.
tourta_karydas.plate: Serve on a platter with a little extra shredded coconut and fresh fruit on the side

steps: Beating the base: Beat the butter with the sugar until fluffy, then add the eggs one at a time along with the lemon zest.
Incorporating wet and dry ingredients: Add the flour with the baking powder alternately with the lemon juice, folding in gently.
Baking: Pour the batter into a 22 cm round pan and bake at 175°C for 35-40 minutes, until golden and a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Slicing into layers: Let cool completely, then cut the cake horizontally into two or three layers.
Cream cheese-lemon filling: Beat the cream cheese with the butter and powdered sugar until light and smooth.
Important: The lemon curd must be completely cold before spreading it on the layers, otherwise it will melt the cream cheese filling and the cake won't hold its shape.
Filling: Spread cream cheese filling and lemon curd alternately between the layers, pressing lightly to set the layers.
Coating and decorating: Cover the entire cake with the remaining cream cheese filling and decorate with lemon slices or zest.
tourta_lemoniou.wine: Sweet Muscat wine or lemon tea
tourta_lemoniou.plate: Serve in slices, chilled, with a lemon slice on the edge of the plate.

steps: Beating the base: Beat the butter with the sugar until fluffy, then add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Incorporating the dry ingredients: Mix the flour with the cocoa and baking powder and add them to the mixture alternately with the milk.
Baking: Pour the batter into a 22 cm round pan and bake at 175°C for 35-40 minutes, until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Slicing into layers: Let the cake cool completely, then cut it horizontally into three equal layers.
Soaking with coffee: Sprinkle each layer with a little espresso so it moistens lightly without becoming soggy.
Mocha buttercream: Beat the butter with the powdered sugar until pale, then gradually add the remaining espresso until smooth.
Important: The buttercream must be whipped at a cool room temperature; if the butter is too soft the cream will 'split' and won't hold its shape on the sides of the cake.
Assembling and finishing: Spread buttercream between the layers and cover the entire cake, dusting the surface with cocoa.
tourta_moka.plate: Serve in slices with a light dusting of cocoa powder and coffee beans as garnish.

steps: Mix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter and press them into the base of a springform tin.
Freeze the base for 20 minutes so it is solid before the ice cream goes on.
Important: Soften the ice cream in the fridge for 15 minutes, not on the counter and never in the microwave. Half-melted ice cream refreezes with ice crystals and loses its texture.
Spread the vanilla ice cream over the base in an even layer and return it to the freezer for 1 hour.
Spread the chocolate ice cream over the frozen first layer and freeze for another 2 hours.
Heat the cream, pour it over the chopped chocolate and stir until you have a smooth glossy ganache.
Important: Let the ganache cool to room temperature before pouring it over. Warm ganache melts a channel straight through the layers.
Pour it over the cake, scatter the toasted almonds and freeze for a final 2 hours.
Move it to the fridge 15 minutes before serving and cut with a hot knife.
tourta_pagoto.plate: Serve in slices showing the layers, with the ganache running down the edges.

steps: Soaking: Soak the trahanas in a little water for 15-30 minutes to let it swell — it cooks more evenly this way.
Sautéing: Sauté briefly in olive oil.
Boiling: Add the stock and tomato, bring to a boil, and stir. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring regularly so it doesn't stick.
Thickening: The trahanas releases starch and the soup thickens naturally. Important: if it thickens too much, add a little hot water.
Serving: In a deep bowl topped with pieces of feta — it melts slightly from the heat.
trahanas.plate: With a piece of feta and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps: Biscuit base: Crush the biscuits and mix with the melted butter. Spread on the bottom of a ring mold and refrigerate.
Hydrating the gelatin: Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.
Dark chocolate mousse: Melt the dark chocolate, whip 1/3 of the cream to soft peaks, and fold in with 2 sheets of drained, melted gelatin.
First layer: Spread the dark chocolate mousse over the base and freeze for 30 minutes until set.
Milk chocolate mousse: Repeat the same process with the milk chocolate and spread it as the second layer, freeze again.
Important: Each mousse layer must be well set in the freezer before adding the next, otherwise the layers will blend together and the three chocolate levels won't be clearly visible.
White chocolate mousse: Make the third mousse with white chocolate the same way and spread it as the final layer, smoothing the surface well.
Sealing and unmolding: Freeze the cake for at least 4 hours or overnight, then run a hot knife around the edge to remove the ring.
tria_sokolata.plate: Served in slices with a little chocolate sauce and shavings of the three chocolates on top.

steps: Chop the chocolate finely and even — large lumps do not melt fully and leave the ganache grainy.
Heat the cream to just below boiling, until small bubbles form at the edges, and never let it boil.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and leave it for 2 minutes without touching it, so the heat spreads evenly.
Stir from the centre outwards in small circles until the ganache turns glossy and smooth.
Important: If the mixture splits and looks oily, add a tablespoon of cold cream and beat hard — this brings it back together.
Stir in the butter and the brandy and refrigerate for 3 hours until firm enough to shape.
Roll into balls with cool hands, working quickly so the ganache does not melt against your palms.
Roll each one in cocoa or ground biscuits and refrigerate for another hour before serving.
troufakia.wine: Brandy or a sweet red wine.
troufakia.plate: Serve in paper cases on a platter, dusted with cocoa.

steps: Cleaning the greens: Wash the greens repeatedly in several changes of water until no grit is left at the bottom of the bowl. Wild greens hold far more soil than they look.
Chopping: Chop them coarsely — greens shrink dramatically and finely chopped ones turn to mush.
Sautéing the onions: Sauté the onion and spring onions in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes, until soft and sweet.
Adding the spices: Important: Add the paprika and the chilli off the heat, or lower it right down. Paprika burns in seconds and turns bitter.
Adding the greens: Add the greens in batches, waiting for each lot to wilt before adding the next, or the pot will overflow.
Adding the fennel: Stir in the chopped wild fennel — this is the herb that gives tsigarelli its Corfiot identity.
Adding the rice: Add the rice and about a cup of hot water, which will thicken the dish as it cooks.
Simmering: Cover and simmer over low heat for 25-30 minutes, until the greens are tender and the liquid has been mostly absorbed.
Finishing: Add the lemon juice off the heat, check the seasoning and let it stand for 10 minutes. It is eaten warm or at room temperature.
tsigarelli.wine: A dry white from Corfu — Kakotrygis — or a fresh Robola.
tsigarelli.plate: Serve in a deep dish with plenty of oil on top, feta on the side and bread.

steps: Cleaning and scoring: Clean the 500g sea bream and dry it well. Make 2-3 diagonal cuts on each side. The scoring helps it cook evenly and lets the flavor penetrate into the flesh.

Salting and aromatics: Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle oregano inside and outside the fish. IMPORTANT: dry the skin thoroughly with paper towels before salting, as moisture prevents the skin from crisping up.
Filling the cavity: Place lemon slices and garlic inside the cavity along with a little thyme. This flavors the fish from within as it roasts.
Preparing the potatoes: Cut the 300g potatoes into thin slices and arrange them on the bottom of the roasting pan. Place the fish on top so the potatoes cook in its juices.
Drizzling: Pour 3 tbsp olive oil and the juice of the remaining lemon over the fish and potatoes.
Roasting: Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes. IMPORTANT: don't overcook it — it's ready as soon as the flesh separates easily from the bone, otherwise it dries out.
Serving: Serve immediately with fresh lemon juice and a little olive oil on top.

ing: Fresh yeast 40 g or dry 14 g
steps: Activating the yeast: Dissolve the yeast in lukewarm milk with a spoonful of sugar and a little flour, and leave it for 15 minutes until it foams.
Important: If it does not foam, the yeast is dead. Start again — nothing later can rescue it.
Grinding the mastic: Grind the mastic tears in a mortar with a pinch of sugar. Important: use no more than 3 tears — mastic in excess turns bitter and medicinal.
Making the dough: Mix the flour with the sugar, the mahleb, the ground mastic, the zest and the salt, then add the yeast mixture and the beaten eggs.
Kneading: Knead for 15 minutes, adding the softened butter little by little, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Important: The dough must pass the windowpane test — stretch a piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing. This is what gives tsoureki its fibrous pull.
First rising: Cover and leave in a warm draught-free spot for 2-3 hours, until it has trebled in size.
Plaiting: Divide into three ropes and plait them, tucking the ends underneath.
Second rising: Let it rise again on the tray for 1-1.5 hours. Important: skipping this second rise gives a dense tsoureki that will not pull apart in strands.
Baking: Brush with egg, scatter almonds and bake at 170°C for 40 minutes, covering it with foil if it browns too fast.
tsoureki.wine: Milk or coffee — traditionally after the Resurrection service.
tsoureki.plate: Serve in slices or torn by hand, with a red egg alongside.
